Its slots line up exactly with the 24-byte disc records: 347 of 347 agree on the type id, so placement is not the reason objects look like the wrong things

0x801b25e5.name: player_state

NOT ordinary walking -- emu/bp14.lua caught it running 69 times in a session, every one in player_state 0x10 or 0x11, while the player walked eight hundred frames without it. tools/movement.py reproduces all 69 exactly

0x80030fcc.name: player_controller

0x80016c08.name: vec_length_2d
0x80016c08.evidence: isqrt((a>>3)^2 + (b>>3)^2) << 3; the slide in player_move divides by it

0x8018faac.name: collision_layers

0x8018fab4.name: current_actor

0x8004da2c.name: actor_select
0x8004da2c.evidence: (actor) -> fills current_actor, current_actor_def and, when the definition's +0x34 has bit 0x10, a second pair from actor[+0x22]. Called with zero it clears all five

0x8004e330.name: actor_move_vertical
0x8004e330.evidence: the half actor_move_horizontal does not do: a state machine on actor[+0xd] -- 0 grounded, 0x10 falling at the definition's own acceleration, 0x20 rising to the surface at 0x64 a frame decaying by 5, 0x30 a ballistic arc from actor[+0x3c] with +0x6a and +0x6c. Every write to an actor's +0x30 in ordinary motion is here

0x8004e094.name: actor_move_3d
0x8004e094.evidence: (velocity triple): moves an actor in all three axes at once and reflects the component that collided; the projectile path

0x80052e5c.name: actor_tick_driver

0x800500a8.name: actor_tick

0x8004dbc8.name: actor_move_horizontal
0x8004dbc8.evidence: the monsters' horizontal move, on current_actor rather than on the player: probes collision at the X- and Z-displaced positions, keeps the MAXIMUM floor (the lowest surface), and rejects the step when the feet would end more than 0x44c above it. Writes X to +0x2c and Z to +0x34; the vertical is actor_move_vertical. 0x8004dca0 is an inner label, not the entry

0x8002ed60.name: player_vertical
0x8002ed60.evidence: the player's height, a state machine on 0x801b25e8. Grounded it is a rate limiter towards the surface collide_surface leaves at 0x801e6474 -- 0x80/0x100/0x200 a frame, placed exactly inside 0x80, a fall past 0x400. States 0x10 and 0x40 are both falls, accelerating 0x50 and 0x28; 0x20 rises from -0x96 by 0xa; 0x50 is the landing recoil and falls through into state 0. emu/bp15.lua caught every store of the player's Y and all of them are in here; tools/movement.py picks the same instruction on 48 of 48

0x8002e3f8.name: player_horizontal
0x8002e3f8.evidence: (angle, distance): dx = cos(angle)*d >> 12 into X, dz = sin(angle)*d >> 12 into Z, committed at 0x8002e580/0x8002e588 if collide_query at 0x31 is clear, else slid along the wall's own facing out of 0x801e6498/0x801e649c. Called twice a frame from 0x8002fda0 and 0x8002fdb4, at the facing and a quarter turn off it

0x801b25e8.name: player_vstate
0x801b25e8.evidence: player_vertical's state byte: 0 grounded, 0x10 and 0x40 falling, 0x20 rising, 0x50 unread

0x801b2656.name: player_vvel
0x801b2656.evidence: s16, the vertical velocity player_vertical integrates; +0x50 a frame in state 0x10, +0xa in 0x20, seeded 0x28 on a fall and -0x96 or -0x12c on a launch

0x801b2602.name: player_dy_applied
0x801b2602.evidence: the height change player_vertical actually applied this frame; zeroed at 0x8002eda0 and set on each moving path

0x80033b10.name: collide_surface
0x80033b10.evidence: (x, y, z, radius, height) -> the nearest surface out of 0x801e6474. Picks the layer from a flat y - 0x500 where collide_wrapper_actor halves the body height; player_vertical asks through this one

0x801b2654.name: player_crouch
0x801b2654.evidence: s16, spent down by state 0x50 of player_vertical after a landing; the state ends when this and player_bob are both non-positive

0x801b2628.name: player_bob
0x801b2628.evidence: s16 the camera dip: half the velocity on every state 0x40 frame, then wound down by state 0x50

0x8002ecbc.name: player_vertical_pre
0x8002ecbc.evidence: called first by each moving state of player_vertical; reads player Y. Not read

0x8002f9bc.name: player_walk
0x8002f9bc.evidence: the speed ramp and the two horizontal calls: forward and back accelerate the s16 at 0x801b2648 by max/4 a frame towards the cap at 0x801b2664, decaying to zero when neither is held

0x8002fe1c.name: player_turn
0x8002fe1c.evidence: first of the four routines the controller runs each frame; reads the button word and the binding table. The turn rate itself is not transcribed

0x801b265c.name: buttons
0x801b265c.evidence: this frame's button word, a set bit meaning pressed. player_controller stores PadRead's return here at 0x80031140 and clear_movement_state masks it down at 0x8002b754; 0x801b265e is last frame's, and a fresh press is set in one and clear in the other

0x801b2612.name: player_facing
0x801b2612.evidence: s16, 0x1000 to the turn. It is a quarter turn off the direction of travel: forward is player_horizontal at facing + 0x400 and strafing at facing, which the recording settled -- at facing 0 the game moves in +Z

0x801b2648.name: player_speed
0x801b2648.evidence: s16 forward speed. Accelerates by max/4 a frame while the button is held and decays by max/8 when it is not, clamping at zero by sign. The two rates differ, and a replay caught it: max/4 both ways overshot on 85 frames of a two-minute session, always while slowing down

0x801b264a.name: player_speed_mag
0x801b264a.evidence: isqrt(forward^2 + strafe^2), formed at 0x8002fd80; player_vertical tests it against 0xc9 when choosing a launch velocity

0x801b2664.name: player_speed_max
0x801b2664.evidence: s32 cap on the walking speed, and the acceleration is a quarter of it. Written only at 0x80031188 and 0x800313e4 -- if walking speed is a stat, that is where it is set

0x80081868.name: bind_forward
0x80081868.evidence: the first of fourteen u16 button masks, one per action; read by player_walk at 0x8002f9c8 and written by apply_control_scheme, which puts 0x1000 in it in all seven movement schemes. WITHDRAWN, the earlier entry here: it called this table key_bindings and read its masks against the raw hardware word, making 0x1000 TRIANGLE and 0x0800 R1. The two halves of that word are swapped by the time PadRead returns it, so 0x1000 is UP and 0x0800 is START. Four independent uses say so: the slot holding 0x0800 is read only by the pause menu, the one holding 0x0100 opens the map, play_movie skips a movie on 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 -- the four face buttons -- and everything on 0x800, and the title menu confirms on 0x20/0x40/0x800 and moves its cursor on 0x1000/0x4000. Under the raw reading those are, in order, R1 opening the menu, L2 the map, the four directions skipping a movie, and the cursor moving on TRIANGLE and CROSS

0x8009a2e0.name: sin_quarter
0x8009a2e0.evidence: 1025 s16 of one quarter wave, 0x1000 to the turn and 4096 to the unit, reflected four ways by 0x80076cc4 (sine) and 0x80076da0 (cosine). Matches round(4096*sin) exactly over a full turn

0x80076cc4.name: game_sin

0x80076da0.name: game_cos

0x80074508.name: game_isqrt
0x80074508.evidence: integer square root through the GTE leading-zero count and a 192-entry table at 0x80096150 -- the library's SquareRoot0, and NOT exact: a perfect square comes back one short, isqrt(40000) = 199. The walking step is speed^2/isqrt(speed^2), so that unit turns a speed of 200 into a step of 201, and a replay using an exact root disagreed with the game on 1394 frames of 3632 for that reason alone

0x80096150.name: isqrt_table
0x80096150.evidence: 192 s16 entries game_isqrt indexes after normalising

0x8002fc94.name: player_step_distances

0x801b264c.name: player_turn_rate

0x801b2652.name: player_bob_phase
0x801b2652.evidence: accumulates the magnitude of the step every frame, wrapped to 0xfff; drives player_bob

0x801b2650.name: player_bob
0x801b2650.evidence: the head bob itself, a function of player_bob_phase

0x8002f298.name: player_bob
0x8002f298.evidence: the tail of player_vertical, grounded only: phase at 0x801b2652 accumulates the step's magnitude every frame and wraps at 0xfff, and the lift at 0x801b2650 is three quarters of |sin(phase) >> 5| -- a rectified sine, so two lifts a stride. The phase accumulates whether or not the step landed, which is why walking into a wall still bobs the camera. Reported from play before it was found in the code

0x801b2640.name: camera_height
0x801b2640.evidence: formed in sync_player_pos at 0x80028e24 as (player Y + 0x640) less the bob and the landing crouch at 0x801b2654

_note_mo_wrapper.name: MO.T entry wrapper
_note_mo_wrapper.evidence: an MO.T entry is not a bare TMD: word 0 is the total size, word 1 a count of 1 to 3, and WORD 2 IS THE OFFSET OF THE TMD, with a table of further offsets from 0x14. Scanning the first 256 bytes for the TMD id found it only for the models that keep it near the front; 53 of level 0's 347 objects, the chests and statues among them, put it thousands of bytes in and were reported as having no model at all

0x801b2610.name: player_pitch
0x801b2610.evidence: s16 immediately before player_facing: where the player is looking up or down, 0x1000 to the turn. Found by logging nine candidates and recording one look up and down -- it was the only one that moved, over 136 values from -596 to +700, and it rests near -190. The first guess, 0x801b2614, reads zero for a whole session and is wrong. POSITIVE IS UP: the resting -190 was read as a downward tilt and the port was built on that, and a player looking up saw it look down

0x80040ae4.name: render_walk
0x80040ae4.evidence: two loops, not one. The first steps the ACTOR table at 0x80185da8 by 0x88 for 200 slots and draws a creature only when its +9 is 1; its model number is the mesh byte at +1 plus 0x80. The second steps object_table by 0x44 for 396 slots, skips a u16 type id of 0xff, clears bit 0x80 of +3 every frame and dispatches on the class byte at +4 -- 0xe9 and 0xe5 are skipped, 0x1f, 0xf0 and 0xf2 each have their own path. The old name here was object_walk, which described only the second half

_note_object_model.name: object type -> model
_note_object_model.evidence: an object of type N uses MO.T[N + 128], and past MO.T's 428 entries the numbering continues into MOF.T. The 128 was MEASURED, not reasoned: a player stood in the game beside the port and named four pairs off the model gallery -- helmet type 34 = model 162, healing grass 104 = 232, save point 227 = 355, bull's head 253 = 381 -- and all four differ by exactly 128. The sizes agree: the grass is 384x211x416 under the rule where MO.T[type] gave it 4176x4096x3808, which is what the player saw as a big white thing. MO.T[type], the previous assumption, had never been checked against anything

0x8001fa60.evidence: keeps 0x800102fa in $s3 and runs a screen of its own; game_main calls it once, straight after the init block, and branches on the result. What OPEN.EXE's menu chose arrives here

0x80018fbc.name: block_zero
0x80018fbc.evidence: (dest, value, count); game_main's first twelve calls clear the object, actor, player and grid tables

0x80040568.name: model_of_type
0x80040568.evidence: (type) -> model number. Below 300 it is type + 0x100 flat. From 300 up a bank is added: (bank << 5) + 0x100, where the bank is the byte at 0x8018fad8, or the one at 0x8018fae4 when 0x8018fad4 is 1 and 0x8018faeb is 1 and it is not 0xff. Since the resource table is offset by 128, type < 300 lands on MO.T[type + 128] -- the rule a player measured off the model gallery, now read off the code -- and type 301 with bank 0 lands on MOF.T[1], the Broken Cart, which is what the gallery said too

0x800405e8.name: model_ptr
0x800405e8.evidence: (model, out): reads model_table[model] and writes it to *out. A model below 0x68 is taken as-is; above that the resource has to answer 1 or 2 to 0x8001947c or the pointer is replaced by zero, which is how a model that is not resident is skipped rather than drawn

0x801a92b0.name: model_table
0x801a92b0.evidence: pointers to loaded models, indexed by the model number model_of_type returns. Objects reach it as type + 0x100 and creatures as their mesh byte + 0x80, so the two numbering schemes meet here

0x800407cc.name: object_in_view
0x800407cc.evidence: (position at record+0x14, record[+0x38], record[+0x39]) -> nonzero to draw. The class 0xf2 path in render_walk skips the object when it answers zero

0x8001796c.name: enter_current_level
0x8001796c.evidence: sets 0x8018fad4 to 1, copies the five bytes of current_level_block to the pending block at 0x8018fae4 and calls level_load. game_main calls it once, after the save screen has answered, and object_trigger is the other route in -- this is the trigger the backlog's cross-level teleport was looking for

0x80017664.name: init_level_state
0x80017664.evidence: registers the nine archives and then clears the level block: 0xff into 0x8018fad9, 0x8018fada and 0x8018fadb, then zero into 0x8018fad4 through 0x8018fadc. game_main calls it in the init chain, so a new game starts from an all-zero level block

0x8007311c.name: cue_sound
0x8007311c.evidence: (id, 0) into 0x8007304c and 0x8006d43c, which splits the id into a high and a low byte and indexes a 43-byte-stride table at 0x801e6cf8. game_main's new-game branch calls it and nothing about it reaches a movie or a model

0x8003c9dc.name: load_data_screen
0x8003c9dc.evidence: the only place \\LOAD.MSG;1 is formed, at 0x8003c9f8. game_main calls it at 0x80014d18, in the init block. LOAD.MSG is one TIM at the root of the disc, 128x160, 4-bit with three CLUTs, bound for VRAM (960,256): the Data Loading card, which comes after OPEN.EXE's own Program Loading

0x800530f8.name: actor_table_build
0x800530f8.evidence: level_load+0x418 hands it link 1 of FDAT entry 3n+1: 200 records of 16 bytes, each copied into a 0x88-byte slot at 0x80185da8 -- category +0, kind +2, flags +5, floor +6, home cell +7/+8, chance +0x0a, yaw +0x20 (negated), fine z/x +0x22/+0x24, height +0x26 -- then actor_copy_kind and actor_stand_at_home. Against a level 0 snapshot, 58 of 58 slots equal in every field but the two men's category

0x8004c1f0.name: actor_activate
0x8004c1f0.evidence: the state machine on actor+9, run by actor_tick_driver on slot k when frame&3 == k&3 (every slot while spawn_anywhere is set): 0 wakes inside (entity+0x0a + 1) cells by category -- 0 in the rim only and on a rand()>>7 roll against actor+0x0a, 1 in the rim, 2 anywhere on a rand()>>4 roll, 3/4 with the leader -- else 2; 1 and 2 fall back to 0 beyond entity+0x0b cells; 3 never changes. Read in full, FORMATS section 17

0x8004b868.name: actor_spawn
0x8004b868.evidence: zeroes +0x40 and +0x44, copies the placed yaw +0x20 into +0x42, stands the actor at home and calls actor_wake; category 3 clears +3

0x8004b698.name: actor_wake
0x8004b698.evidence: +9 = 1, clears the AI bytes +0x0c..+0x11 and +0x18, a random yaw rand()>>3 into +0x42 unless actor+5 bit 0 is set, then marks its cells through grid_query_area

0x8004b624.name: actor_copy_kind
0x8004b624.evidence: copies model, +0x1a, radius (entity+0x12), height (entity+0x14), flags (entity+0x34) and +0x32 out of the entity record the actor's +2 names

0x8004b560.name: actor_stand_at_home
0x8004b560.evidence: x = cell x<<11 + fine x, z likewise, y = collide_at_cell on floor actor+6 (0 if not negative), then the base height instead under flag 0x400, plus the height +0x26 unless flag 0x10. Reproduces a level 0 snapshot's 54 idle actors to the unit

0x8004b770.name: actor_retire
0x8004b770.evidence: +9 = 3 and back home; a category-1 death, and nothing ever changes 3 again

0x8004b8c4.name: actor_spawn_slot
0x8004b8c4.evidence: (slot) -> actor_spawn on that slot, whatever its distance or category; no jal reaches it, so it is called through a table

0x8004b794.name: actors_retire_marked
0x8004b794.evidence: every category-1 actor that is up, whose +0x0c reads 0xf003xxxx and whose +0x70 is set or +0x18 exceeds 0x800, goes through the hook at (*0x8018fae0)+0x4c and then actor_retire; called by player_controller, 0x80047010 and 0x8005c864

0x80016ec8.name: in_range
0x80016ec8.evidence: (pos*, x, y, z, r, top, own) -> distance or -1: |dx|,|dz| <= r, then SquareRoot0 of (dx>>3)^2+(dz>>3)^2, shifted back up by 3, <= r; y = 0xffff skips the height overlap test

0x8004d644.name: actor_spot_taken
0x8004d644.evidence: (x, y, z, radius, height) -> the first other actor that is up (+9 == 1) and overlaps, radius on radius and height on height, or -1. The activator asks it before every spawn

0x8005efd4.name: level_state_write

0x800796c0.name: rand
0x800796c0.evidence: BIOS A0:2F thunk: next = next*0x41c64e6d + 0x3039, returns (next>>16) & 0x7fff

0x801b24f2.name: spawn_anywhere
